## EH1 consumed attempt: invalid primary, complete post-hoc trace

EH1 later launched once from clean pushed source
`fad011bbdca6b2b81791058abee3901bcda0ac8a`. Both fixed arms completed all 472
steps, but the process exited `1` because the frozen primary evaluator rejected
the report. The identity is consumed and closed; it may not be rerun, repaired,
rethresholded, or have either arm replaced.

The retained 79,950,421-byte report is
`<evidence-root>\c6-rapier-bw19v-velocity-only-eh1-fad011b\report.json`,

`cdbcebc11eb727f9d24be6900788f6fd180cf8fc27a7df71780dc7d1921f6fa5`.
It remains `ok=false`. Its four failures are step-zero receipt failures plus
residual-counter recomputation failures for both arms.

The diagnosis found two cases where the hand-authored perfect synthetic report
agreed with its evaluator but not with the production path:

1. Both expected invented profile ID
   `rapier_force_based_velocity_only_target_v1`; production and every pinned v4
   authority use `rapier_force_based_velocity_only_v1`.

   change. In EH1-B, 1,822 residuals were nonzero before the complete-command
   clamp, while 1,759 changed the final host velocity; 63 were absorbed by
   saturation.

The second defect emerged only after correcting the profile expectation:
because the original evaluator stopped at step zero, its reported residual
recomputation errors did not reveal whether a deeper count mismatch existed.
The post-hoc auditor therefore did not stop at the first plausible explanation.
It corrected the effective-count reconstruction and added a synthetic case in
which a nonzero bounded residual is deliberately absorbed by the final clamp.

The immutable post-hoc diagnostic, SHA-256
`6f6c0fefe33b86fd0388101194344105b5e2fd1e6f184a55b8848ea1fdc523fa`,
reuses the complete real-report gate and finds zero corrected counterfactual
integrity failures. Both 472-step traces contain no declared event or torso

`0.423656 m`/`0.122804 rad`. All controller, composition, nonfinite,
application, motor-field, and impulse-limit integrity counters are zero.

Those are retained post-hoc development observations only. They do not change

## Post-baseline addition: turning and multi-engine live debugging

Command-conditioned turning is now ordered as the first new quadruped
locomotion capability after the base straight-walking engine-neutral slice.
It must enter the portable SDK as a versioned task-frame command with exact
zero-command backward compatibility, not as a hidden per-engine gait preset.
The first bounded claim should cover signed gentle left/right arcs and
straight-to-turn-to-straight transitions. Pivot turns, reversing arcs,
waypoint following, navigation, and turning under disturbances remain separate
successors.

Turning evaluation must replace the straight-path lateral corridor only where
the command intentionally requests a curve. Those cells require frozen
curve-relative cross-track, yaw/curvature response, forward-progress, slip,
contact, stability, saturation, and recovery-to-straight gates. Zero-command
cells retain the existing straight-line drift gate as a regression control.
Every physical turning campaign still requires a new identity, prospective
thresholds, full synthetic whole-gate preflight, signed pairs, fresh seeds,
and host-specific evidence before any cross-engine claim.

The operator workbench also has a prospective implementation TODO: make
Rapier/Parry and MuJoCo real development-world launch choices. Rapier must run
through the actual `sdk/adapters/rapier` host and stream read-only physical
state to the 3D observer; MuJoCo must run through its actual adapter/host or
native viewer. Each overlay must display the true engine/version/configuration
identity, and an executable negative control must prove that neither selection
silently falls back to Godot/Jolt.

These future viewers are debuggers, not publication shortcuts. Their ordinary
runs remain clearly nonretained and `development_only`; they may reveal a
failure and motivate a new preregistration, but they grant no walking,
turning, C6, equivalence, robustness, selector, validation, or release
authority by themselves. Unopened frozen candidates remain unavailable to the
casual viewer until their one-shot campaign closes.

## 2026-08-01 BW23Y yaw-authority development checkpoint

The BW21L/BW22L diagnostics did not support stronger cross-track proportional
or velocity feedback. Stronger P=1.5 increased paired regressions, and the
doubled velocity term increased saturation without fixing the difficult
mid-friction behavior. The next mechanism was therefore deliberately
orthogonal: sporespore_balanced_wave_bw23y_b_v1 preserves the complete
BW15F-B profile and changes only yaw_error_stride_gain_per_rad from 1.3 to
1.0. An exhaustive serialized profile test removes policy identity and that
one coefficient, then requires every remaining field to be exactly equal.

The zero-world policy inspector
sdk/core/examples/inspect_policy_profile.rs binds the actual engine-neutral
profile rather than a hand-copied description. At the reference descriptor,
the BW23Y profile SHA-256 is
sha256:d345d9607bed545ee6c58a20055cd6258f38ed581dd3d9f6490a9ae7f1a57570.
The inspector builds no world, changes no physics state, and exposes no
locomotion outcome.

The first attempted physical development probe was invalid. The GDScript
allowlists and release DLL included BW23Y, but Godot's editor/headless host
loads the .gdextension windows.debug artifact. That debug DLL was stale, so
the adapter stayed in the legacy shadow identity and never acquired full SDK
authority. One real world had been opened, but its motion values are
inadmissible as candidate diagnostics: SDK steps, native SDK motor writes, and
mechanism authority were all zero.

sdk/run_balanced_wave_bw23y_yaw_gain_development_preflight.ps1 turns that
failure into an executable guard. Standalone use rebuilds the exact debug DLL
Godot will load, inspects the canonical policy digest, rejects an unexposed
value/seed canary, and exercises the complete selected-policy authority start
plus declared runtime boundary. Its passing marker is:

~~~text
BW23Y_YAW_GAIN_DEVELOPMENT_PREFLIGHT_PASS profile_sha256=sha256:d345d9607bed545ee6c58a20055cd6258f38ed581dd3d9f6490a9ae7f1a57570 yaw_gain=1 unexposed_canary=True authority_scope=post_settle_full worlds=0 outcomes_exposed=False physical_authority=False
~~~

Only after that pass were three nonretained real Godot/Jolt development worlds
opened, all on already outcome-exposed BW22L profiles and seeds:

| Profile/seed | BW22L-A exposed result | BW23Y development result | BW23Y saturation | BW23Y final lateral | BW23Y cumulative error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| mu 0.81 / 24011 | fail | fail | 296 | 0.1143 m | 1.7490 m*s |
| mu 0.81 / 24013 | fail | pass | 283 | 0.0813 m | 2.0359 m*s |
| mu 0.57 / 24012 | pass | pass | 63 | 0.0665 m | 0.8686 m*s |

All three probe receipts passed the role/harness gate, used
post_settle_full authority, produced more than 20,000 native SDK motor writes,
reported no SDK failure codes, and granted no selection, validation,
retention, or physical-acceptance authority. Against the same exposed cells,
the baseline passed 1/3 and BW23Y passed 2/3. The two difficult mu=0.81 cells
had substantially less saturation and better final lateral recovery. The
already-good mu=0.57 cell remained walking but became less precise: cumulative
error rose from about 0.46 to 0.8686 m*s and saturation from 51 to 63.

The defensible interpretation is a mixed development signal, not promotion.
Lower yaw-to-stride authority may trade tight easy-case correction for less
overshoot and better difficult-case recovery. BW23Y now warrants a distinct
paired control/candidate campaign; it has not established superiority,
walking acceptance, or material robustness. The next campaign must first
publish newly characterized, outcome-unexposed material values, then use fresh
seeds and a new source/evidence identity. Its complete zero-world evaluator
must consume real-shaped candidate, control, safety, and negative-walking
receipts and reject the leaked walking dictionary, missing coefficient,
incomplete safety schema, and stale-host-artifact defect families before any
fresh locomotion world opens.

## 2026-08-05: GJTP1 makes the Godot native route single-pass and pre-world pinned

The live-code audit after BW32N found that the Godot GDExtension's generic
JSON helper executed every pure C-ABI operation once to obtain its output size
and a second time to obtain the bytes. For a balanced-wave tick, each native
invocation parses the full descriptor/state/memory request, recompiles the
bounded morphology, constructs the named controller, steps it, and serializes
the result. This duplicated native controller work on every authority
observation.

GJTP1 replaces the mandatory size query with a `16,384`-byte preallocated
output. The normal path has exactly one native invocation; a genuinely larger
output may receive one exact-size retry after `SS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`. It keeps
the JSON boundary and every controller, morphology, observation, actuation,
physics, solver, seed, horizon, threshold, selector, and closed-campaign
semantic unchanged. The exact execution identity is
`sporespore_godot_json_preallocated_single_pass_v1`.

The route cannot be selected silently. The native class reports a versioned
runtime contract. The GDScript adapter requires the exact method, version,
capacity, invocation count, retry limit, JSON modes, and zero-authority fields
before descriptor compilation. Both shared real-physics runners repeat that
handshake before any fixture construction or scene-tree insertion and retain
the contract in preflight and physical receipts. Missing, stale, or tampered
identity fails with zero worlds. The durable declaration is
[`../sdk/godot_jolt_transport_execution_contract.json`](../sdk/godot_jolt_transport_execution_contract.json),
and its source and live-GDExtension negative canaries are mandatory under
`sdk/run_conformance.ps1`.

All future Godot/Jolt physical declarations must pin this transport version,

runner source digests, and the built DLL digest. A later transport revision
requires a new version and must fail old preflights before physics. GJTP1 has

rough-terrain, push, noise, turning, self-righting, morphology,
continuous-domain, cross-engine, release, completed-SDK, or physical

## 2026-09-04 QSDK-R10F continuous passive-recovery successor design

The
[R10F design](../sdk/qsdk_r10f_continuous_passive_fall_recovery_successor_design_v1.json)
does not try to repair R10E-L3 after observing it. It asks a different
prospective question: can the exact selected S169 body first stand, walk under
BW5R-B, receive the same source-measured native `0.25 N s` lateral kick, pass
through an unactuated prone-confirmation interval, stand with V6, and then
start a fresh BW5R-B session that resumes forward movement—all without
rebuilding the body or writing its state?

This requires a new facade rather than reusing the old walking scene as though
it were physically identical. The old scene has different limb shapes,
different callback coverage, and friction `0.95`; the recovery-native body has
all nine bodies under callback-aware state and retains its rough friction `1.8`
profile. Policy identity and actuator caps remain frozen even though their host
fixture changes.

The recovery contract is extended with an honest local epoch. Global completed
step `G` never restarts. The coherent completed post-kick boundary is `E`, and
the recovery module sees local step `L = G - E`. All nine live body states and
the complete live energy at `E` are retained before any recovery command for
`E+1`. The kick is not counted as recovery work; its application and immediate
native effect remain in a separate receipt. No transform, velocity, contact,
or solver-state reset is permitted.

The maximum active arm is 3,841 solver steps: up to 1,200 for the canonical
standing precondition, 720 walking-prefix steps, one kick-effect step, up to
1,200 post-kick recovery-epoch steps including prone confirmation, and 720
walking-resume steps. Development seed `40200` has two arms; held-out seeds
`40201`-`40203` stay inaccessible until a positive development result and a
new finite-decision graph exist.

The
[zero-world design audit](../sdk/conformance/qsdk_r10f_continuous_passive_fall_recovery_successor_design.py)
passes with 15 bound authorities, 35 reopened R10E-L3 evidence files totaling
`79,688,410` bytes, 48 implementation-seam markers, 262 mutation refusals, and
zero physical counters. R10F is event-triggered passive recovery. It does not
implement or claim force sensing, force-aware bracing, or real-time force-aware
recovery; that broader capability remains SDK2 work. Source implementation and
zero-world qualification come next. No world is authorized by this design.

## 2026-09-04 QSDK-R10F-L6 precondition pair-barrier implementation

L6 now implements the prospective barrier without changing either controller.
The active kick arm and matched no-kick arm each retain their own unchanged V6
terminal source. If one becomes ready first, that world keeps taking measured
solver steps with every hinge motor disabled and every target velocity zero
while the other continues the ordinary V6 precondition. Once both are ready,
both take one no-actuation release frame and begin fresh BW5R-B walking-prefix
sessions at the next shared global boundary.

This matters because an engine can advance two isolated worlds on the same
host frames without making their floating-point threshold crossings identical.
L6 keeps the shared experimental clock while removing that unnecessary
assumption. It does not pause a world, copy readiness, change a threshold,
rewrite a body, alter the kick, or use the later outcome to repair the earlier
precondition.

The 104-path v7 development audit passes 31 source tests, 17 positive
compositions, and 92 forced failures. The focused barrier cases cover both
one-arm-first orders, same-frame completion, multi-frame waiting, valid wait
and release applications, and twelve pair/application corruptions. Future
authority and closure tools reject 18 and 25 mutations. Real Godot parse and
detached zero-world execution pass with zero physical activity.

No official v7 qualification or execution authority exists yet. The source
must be sealed and pushed before the one allowed qualification, then the
freeze/authority graph must be committed and checked before at most one new
development route ghost. Kick/push recovery, force-aware recovery, M07, M20,
and scores `14/20` and `14/25` remain unchanged.

walking session through an explicit facade-owned transition. The transition

retains its content digest before the unchanged first BW5R-B command. It and

frame or body intervention is introduced and the preceding L11 release remains
motors-disabled exactly as observed.

from the unchanged published profile. The handoff retains each selected
binary32 host value and its adjacent-value maximality proof, then supplies the
complete selected-host map to the shared adapter's existing override. The
shared adapter itself, its enable behavior, and the published cap profile do
not change. There is no empirical margin, tolerance, clamp, threshold change,
or outcome-derived correction.

The worker retains one handoff per fresh session. The pair evaluator and
future closer require its exact model, session, evaluation-segment, step, motor
population, cap population, projection digests, and ordering. Prefix must be
followed by matched continuation in the no-kick child and by walking resume in
the kick child. Missing, duplicate, crossed, disabled, nonzero, partial,
reordered, published-as-host, arbitrary-lower, adjacent-higher, stale-digest,
and outcome-bearing receipts fail. A precondition-negative child must retain
neither a walking session nor a handoff.

L12 source `0d41c01a80985338aa411ee3049fcdab44a1e63c` passed its one
official zero-world qualification. Qualification-only v13 freeze
`6baeb8738e1b3103aca3900df3090dd2c60a1d67` and separate authority

model and world, completed the unchanged V6 stand at step 240, and completed
the motors-disabled release at 241. On planned walking step 242, L12's new
handoff enabled all eight motors at zero target, completed all 24 pre-command
motor reads, and bound the eight exact R69 host-cap projections. The native
BW5R-B session step, full-authority application, and post-application motor
population readback all succeeded. This validates the ownership handoff itself
on the production route.

Before a walking intent could be retained or a walking solver frame could run,
the ledger returned `QSDK_R10F_WALKING_LEDGER_IDENTITY_INVALID`. The active
child, second world, kick, passive fall, recovery, resumed walk, and behavior
evaluator never ran. Total execution was one model, one world, and 241 solver
steps.

The 9,084-byte

at SHA-256
`b3ca434ee589d283077d1d4e20d3681a3368e07af1824c5926151c20d1f30e21`

The durable zero-world diagnosis receipt is 9,375 bytes at SHA-256
`ccbe2dbe3a78d8613f5d90ea7d22fa0eca508d76dc9cfe716f9fe9d1e1a87755`
under

R69 caps, and eight detached hinge-parameter containers without a model, body,
world, native read, or solver step.

That production-shaped control passes every deterministic ledger identity
field. The source's failure ordering therefore isolates the live failure to the
one input-dependent check that re-created the native controller-receipt digest
from a Godot dictionary after `JSON.parse_string`. The exact unequal digest
strings were not retained because the L12 abort serializer omitted the step
sources; this remains a deductive isolation, not a direct pairwise digest
measurement. An ideal controller receipt did round-trip with equal digest
`e516935d8da34a42d14c663d0551b1ecc716805dfe3d0a37ce3297092bcab2aa`,
and 4,096 deterministic scalar probes produced zero canonical digest changes.
Those controls do not reproduce the input-dependent live receipt and cannot
authorize post-parse rehash as proof about the unparsed response.

When the isolated identity predicate is bypassed, the same control reaches
`QSDK_R10F_WALKING_LEDGER_ROW_INVALID:0`. The portable controller emits a
binary64 target; Godot stores the target motor parameter as binary32. L12's row
requires those two representations to compare exactly. The observed zero-world
differences reach `7.391781098320394e-08 rad/s`, while all eight R69 cap
projections remain exact. This is the deterministic next pre-solver defect, not
a second observed physical failure or evidence for changing the command,
tolerance, or cap.

2. Retain the unchanged binary64 controller target and its exact binary32

3. Replace the opaque ledger failure with a v2 named predicate vector and
